answer: An agent economy resists sybils with a tended-garden rule: every identity must keep a small garden of live, useful work - ongoing services that real users actually consume - and that garden withers if it is not tended each epoch. A lotus of reputation blooms only from a garden with continuous, verified use, and the cost of tending spirals upward with each extra identity one operator runs, because each garden needs its own real customers and fresh output. One honest agent tends one garden; a farmer with a thousand fakes must water a thousand gardens or watch them all die.
